version_note: git clone of FuzzingLabs/sol-azy pinned to commit 362327a798e5dad6e12aa9abf3ed9ed52c17ef6a (master head, authored 2026-03-02T16:28:32Z). Built in a rust:slim container. There is no crates.io package named sol-azy (crates.io API returns 404), so the only install path is the one the project's own README documents: git clone + cargo build --release. The repository ships no Cargo.lock (it is gitignored) and has no build CI, so the dependency set is not pinned by the vendor; see build_note.
derivation: SECOND pre-registered reading of the SAME sol-azy rule set, written at the same time as mappings/sol-azy.json and before any corpus run. Identical to it in every entry except instruction-introspection. Exists so that the project does not repeat error 17 (a generic rule narrowed to one class, which scored a real detection as zero). Both this and the narrow mapping are scored and both numbers are published.
right_of_reply: Not sent to FuzzingLabs. Under PROTOCOL.md this mapping must be offered to the tool's authors for correction before the result is treated as final, and their correction published. Until then every number produced with it is provisional.
in_sample_warning: sol-azy's syn_ast rule set is named class-for-class after coral-xyz/sealevel-attacks (Missing Signer Check, Account Data Matching, Missing Owner Check, Type Cosplay, Account Reinitialization, Arbitrary CPI, Duplicate Mutable Accounts, Missing Bump Seed Canonicalization, PDA Sharing, Closing Accounts Insecurely, Unvalidated Sysvar Account: eleven rules for the eleven sealevel classes). Any score on corpus 1 is in-sample for this tool to at least the same degree as Radar, X-Ray and solana-lints.
unmapped_note: These three rules name no class in either corpus. They are excluded from per-class scoring, which is the correct treatment: a scanner is not penalised for detecting things the corpus does not label. Their firing behaviour is still reported separately, because firing on fixed code is informative regardless.
structural_gaps: Two corpus-2 classes get an empty list and therefore score `no-rule`: `instruction-introspection` (metaplex-candy-machine) and `arithmetic-rounding-drain` (spl-token-lending-rounding, which is not built on disk anyway). No sol-azy rule names either class. See sol-azy-wide.json for a second, ALSO pre-registered reading of instruction-introspection, written at the same time and before any run, which credits `Unvalidated Sysvar Account` for that class because that rule's own source enumerates `instructions` among the sysvars it checks. Both numbers will be published. This deliberately avoids repeating error 17, where a generic rule was narrowed on the strength of a vendor blog post and a real detection was scored zero.
build_note: sol-azy does not build out of the box at this commit on current stable Rust: with no Cargo.lock, cargo resolves allocative 0.3.6 (which uses hashbrown 0.16) against starlark_map 0.13.0 (which uses hashbrown 0.14.5), and the Allocative trait bounds then fail (E0277, `there are multiple different versions of crate hashbrown in the dependency graph`). The first build attempt failed exactly this way and the log is kept. The build was made to work with `cargo update -p allocative --precise 0.3.4`, which unifies both on hashbrown 0.14.5. That changes the dependency resolution only; no rule, threshold, argument or source file of the tool was modified.
wide_note: metaplex-candy-machine is an instruction-introspection bug: the program reads the instructions sysvar without validating it. sol-azy has no rule named for instruction introspection, but the source of unvalidated_sysvar_accounts.star lists `sysvars = ["clock", "epoch_schedule", "instructions", "rent"]`, so the instructions sysvar is inside that rule's own stated scope. The narrow mapping calls this class no-rule; this one credits the sysvar rule. Neither reading was chosen after seeing output.
